title: Adaptive Tenant QoS and Traffic Shaping for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Leah Morgan
description: PRD for an adaptive tenant Quality-of-Service (QoS) and traffic-shaping layer on Redwood Dedicated that provides predictable latency and fair cost allocation during sustained high utilization and transient bursts. This feature complements existing reserved pools and autoscaling by introducing per-tenant workload classes, soft eviction rules, and dynamic shaping that preserves SLOs for critical tenants while allowing safe, measurable burst behavior for lower-priority workloads.
background: Customers running Redwood Dedicated have asked for stronger guarantees that a noisy tenant or workload won't degrade latency for others during constrained capacity windows. Existing reserved pools + autoscaling address baseline isolation but lack granular runtime shaping and transparent eviction behavior when capacity is exhausted. Engineering has prototypes for queue-based shaping and token-level throttles; this PRD scopes product requirements and acceptance criteria for an initial MVP and a phased rollout.
goals: Provide per-tenant workload classes (Critical | Business | BestEffort) that map to runtime shaping policies
Implement a traffic-shaping service (in control plane) that can apply queueing and token-bucket limits at routing time to prevent head-of-line blocking
Introduce a soft eviction policy that preemptively rejects or throttles BestEffort requests under severe contention, with transparent signals and analytics
Expose QoS configuration and runtime metrics in Redwood Console and API for visibility and billing attribution
Ensure behavior integrates with reserved pools, autoscaling, and existing fallback policies without regressing latency SLOs for Critical workloads
non_goals: Do not introduce hard preemption of active KV cache entries in the MVP
Not building a complete per-model compiler-level optimization — focus is on routing + shaping and soft eviction
Do not change billing model in the MVP; charge changes to be considered separately
requirements: REQ-1: Define workload classes and default mappings: Critical, Business, BestEffort. Customers can override per-route.
REQ-2: Control-plane API to set tenant QoS policy, including per-class max concurrent requests, burst window, and reorder priority.
REQ-3: Runtime shaping middleware must be able to apply: token-bucket throttles, queueing with max queue time, and request rejection with configurable status and retry-after headers.
REQ-4: Soft eviction policy: when cluster-level available capacity drops below a threshold, BestEffort queued requests are rejected or downgraded; Business workloads are throttled before Critical.
REQ-5: Console: QoS dashboard showing current policy, queue depth, rejected request counts, latency percentiles by workload class, and per-tenant cost impact estimates.
REQ-6: Observability: emit structured events for shaping decisions (throttle, queue, reject), and correlate with model and route for debugging and billing reconciliation.
REQ-7: Compatibility: shaping layer must respect autoscaling signals and reserved pool guarantees; autoscaler should consider both in scaling triggers.
REQ-8: UX: sensible defaults and migration path for existing tenants (default mapping to Business), and API validation to prevent accidental denial-of-service configurations.
REQ-9: Security/compliance: shaping control APIs must be RBAC-protected and audited; changes recorded in audit logs for Private deployments.
REQ-10: Graceful rollout flags and canarying for customers to opt into adaptive shaping per cluster or pool
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Create API endpoints to assign per-route workload class and to set per-tenant shaping parameters; POST/GET/PUT validated and RBAC-protected
AC-2: Under a simulated 70% baseline utilization + 3x burst of BestEffort traffic, Critical p50 latency must not increase more than 10% from baseline in 95% of test runs
AC-3: When capacity falls below configured threshold, BestEffort requests are rejected with 429 and a Retry-After header; reject rate and reasons appear in Console within 30s
AC-4: Console shows live queue depth, per-class latency P50/P95/P99, and a historical chart for rejected/throttled requests for the last 24h
AC-5: Autoscaler integration: when shaping is active, autoscaler still scales to meet Critical demand; a test harness demonstrates autoscaler decision unaffected by BestEffort overload
AC-6: Logging: shaping events include tenant, route, model, workload_class, action, and token counts; events are queryable in the observability backend within 60s
AC-7: Migration: enabling default mapping does not change behavior for existing tenants marked as 'reserved-pool' in >= 99% of sampled requests
AC-8: Security: all changes to QoS policies are present in audit log and show user and timestamp
success_metrics: S-1: Reduction in cross-tenant latency regressions caused by noisy neighbors by >= 80% in 30-day post-launch window
S-2: Mean number of customer support incidents about Dedicated capacity contention falls by 50% in first quarter
S-3: Adoption: 40% of Dedicated customers configure at least one workload class within 90 days of availability
S-4: Fraction of rejected BestEffort tokens that would have caused Critical latency >10% reduced to <5% after tuning
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Canary): Expose QoS API + Console read-only views to internal tenants; enable shaping in a single test cluster
Phase 1 (Pilot): Opt-in pilot with 5 external customers representing three verticals; enable shaping for BestEffort only; collect metrics and feedback
Phase 2 (General Availability): Default mapping to Business for new tenants, UI to opt-in/override; enable soft eviction; multi-cluster rollout with feature flag
Phase 3 (Refinements): Add per-route cost attribution changes and premium QoS controls for enterprise customers
dependencies: ENG-9072: Runtime middleware hooks for request routing (queueing + token counters)
ENG-9121: Autoscaler integration work to consider shaping signals
ENG-8994: Console telemetry pipeline to surface shaping events
SEC-312: RBAC + audit logging endpoints for control-plane changes
LEGAL-88: Review of audit retention and compliance requirements for Private deployments
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overly aggressive shaping could cause customer outages. Mitigation: conservative defaults, staged pilot, and immediate rollback flags
Risk: Mis-attribution of cost due to rejections. Mitigation: ensure observability emits tokens attempted vs accepted; update billing docs before GA
Risk: Complex interplay with autoscaling leads to oscillations. Mitigation: implement damping in autoscaler and test with load-generator against a staging cluster
Risk: Customers confused by soft eviction behavior. Mitigation: provide in-console simulation tool and clear docs with examples
stakeholders: Eng: Rajesh Patel (platform lead), Maria Gomez (runtime)
open_questions: Q1: Should token-bucket limits be measured per-route or per-tenant for initial MVP? (engineering prefers per-route for granularity)
Q2: What default thresholds for queue time and max queue length give the best UX across model sizes?
Q3: Do we need an explicit billing contract change for customers who want guaranteed Critical headroom?
Q4: How should shaping interact with function/tool-calling where latency expectations differ?
decision_log: 2026-02-25: Decided on three workload classes (Critical, Business, BestEffort) for MVP
2026-03-03: Chose control-plane shaping with queueing and token-bucket throttles instead of kernel-level preemption for lower risk
2026-03-10: Require audit logging and RBAC for QoS API changes for Private deployments
notes: Prototype throughput tests indicate token-bucket shaping adds <2% CPU overhead to router path for typical qps
We will reuse the existing fallback policy UI for customers that want auto-fallback to hosted models when capacity constrained
Consider linking this with Optimize recommendations: surface suggestions for workload class assignment based on observed traffic patterns
timeline: Mar 2026: Finalize API schema and control-plane design
Apr 2026: Implement runtime middleware + basic Console charts (Phase 0)
May 2026: Pilot with select customers and iterate
Jun 2026: GA rollout to all Dedicated customers
